QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_24

question.text: A Nifty option is exercised and the settlement value is Rs 2,50,000. Per the Equity Derivatives workbook, what is the Securities Transaction Tax (STT) payable on this exercised option, and who pays it?

answer.text: Rs 312.50, payable by the purchaser — STT on an exercised option is 0.125% of the settlement (intrinsic) value (0.125% × Rs 2,50,000)
Rs 250, payable by the seller, at 0.10% of settlement value
Rs 50, payable by the seller, at 0.02% of settlement value (the rate applicable to futures)
Rs 500, combining buyer and seller STT rates

explanation.text: The Logic: The Equity Derivatives workbook distinguishes between normal sale of an option and exercise of an option. Normal sale of an option attracts STT of 0.10% on the option premium, payable by the seller. Sale of an option where the option is exercised attracts STT of 0.125% on the settlement (intrinsic) value, payable by the purchaser. Here, the option is exercised with settlement value Rs 2,50,000, so STT = 0.125% × Rs 2,50,000 = Rs 312.50, paid by the purchaser. The Trap: The 0.10% seller-paid rate applies to a non-exercised option sale, not to exercise. The 0.02% rate is for futures, not options. Combining both sides into 0.20% is not how STT is levied. Note: Because the exercise rate is materially higher and is computed on settlement value rather than premium, many traders prefer to square off deep in-the-money options before expiry rather than allow them to be exercised.
